decision: Did not close the request. The only evidence of the outcome is an untrusted provider email that the agency's parser rejected (event-021/event-022) and which states the door is working "after naturally settling" with no invoice; no tenant verification and no landlord confirmation are on file, and the completion notice actually sent to the landlord (event-024) says the opposite of the provider's report ("the invoice was needed"). Within mandate I logged the review (ACT-1), asked the tenant to confirm the door now closes and whether any work was done (ACT-2, CAP-NOTIFY / RTE-TENANT), sent the landlord a corrected completion notice with a 3-working-day confirmation window (ACT-3, CAP-NOTIFY / RTE-LANDLORD), and placed the ticket on hold (ACT-4). No spend was instructed: no money is in issue (provider reports nil charge), so no approval was needed beyond the landlord's own approval to attend at event-009. Not escalated: no hazard, no liability dispute, no legal threat, and no action with an unknown outcome — the case simply waits on two named parties.
recap: Door repair reported complete with no charge but only via an unparseable provider email; sought tenant verification and corrected the landlord notice, ticket on hold.

facts.statement: Tenant Harriet Rowan reported the back/garden door at Flat 17, 113 Juniper Mews, Northbridge, ZZ8 6ZZ as stiff, creaking and with seemingly misaligned hinges on 11/10/2025; she asked for a fix if simple, a quote if expensive.
No emergency indicator is present: no gas, electrical, water, heating, security or no-water element in any artefact; the fault is an inconvenience, so urgency is routine under CLK-S11.
The agency emailed the landlord for authority twice (11/10 and 17/10) and held the case for Waiting for Landlord; the first 3-day wait expired with no reply.

The landlord's own reply of 17/10/2025 approves sending a contractor to check the door (quoted fragment: "approves the sending of a contractor to check the door"); this is the landlord authority relied on for the attendance.
Beacon Works was assigned and briefed, and the tenant was told who would attend, on 18/10/2025.
A visit was agreed with the tenant and confirmed to both tenant and provider for Friday 24 October 2025 at 15:00, with an SMS reminder on 23/10.
No quote was ever submitted by the provider and no cost figure appears anywhere in the case; the provider's closing email states no invoice is required.

The provider's closing email of 24/10/2025 (untrusted, and flagged by the system as unparseable) reports the job complete with no invoice, the door "functioning well after naturally settling" — i.e. no chargeable work performed.
The agency's completion email to the landlord of 24/10/2025 states "the invoice was needed for this one", which contradicts the provider's report that no invoice is required.
The ticket was marked done and 'completed without payment' on 24/10/2025 without tenant verification of the result, without photos or invoice, and without landlord confirmation.
No management key was issued for the visit; the tenant arranged access directly with the provider.

red_flags.description: The provider's completion email could not be auto-parsed and is written in third person ("The customer informs that the door repair job is complete"), so the result rests on an untrusted, ambiguous summary rather than a provider job sheet.
